deep.reconstruction:
The upper half of the page draws composable configurations of cells in a strict 2-category and pairs each one with a small rectangular grid recording its shape.

(i) Top row: subdivided segments with 2, 3 and 4 pieces. These are strings of composable 1-cells, i.e. the ordinals [2], [3], [4] (Δ_n viewed as a path).

(ii) Hatched lens-shaped 2-cells, each with a grid:
- a single lens cut by a middle 1-cell, with a 2-box grid: two vertically composable 2-cells;
- two lenses side by side, with a 1×2 grid: two horizontally composable 2-cells;
- a circle cut by two arcs (three stacked 2-cells), with a 3-box column: vertical composition of three cells;
- three lenses in a row, with a 1×3 grid: horizontal composition of three cells;
- at the bottom, two circles glued at a point, each with a middle line, with a 2×2 grid: the interchange (Godement) configuration of four 2-cells.

In modern terms these are the shapes [m; n_1,…,n_m] of Joyal's cell category Θ_2, restricted to the 'rectangular' case n_1=…=n_m=n. In that case the shape is coded by the product of ordinals Δ_m × Δ_n, i.e. a grid.

The next page confirms this. It takes products Δ_{n_1}×…×Δ_{n_r} and Δ_n×Δ_{n'}, and filters them: F_0 = ∂Δ_{n'}, F_1 = Fl(Δ_n)×∂Δ_{n'}, F_2 = Fl(Δ_n)×Fl(Δ_{n'}). It also writes source/target and unit maps F_0 ⇇ F_1 ⇇ F_2 and coherence data a, l, r. So the program is to present the free 2-category (or a cellular, 'n-fold category' structure) on a product of ordinals or categories, filtered by cell dimension. This is the combinatorics behind lax/Gray-type products and the nerve of 2-categories.

The lower half is a schematic chain of categories of 'models' or base categories:
(Ss ?) ↪ (Cat) ⇄ (Prédérivateurs) → (Ord) → (Maquettes; 'Triades' crossed out).
'Prédériv' is evidently prederivators, i.e. 2-functors Cat^op → Cat. Cat sits inside them via representables.

Below, 'F_x → F_y, x ≤ y' denotes a diagram indexed by an ordered set: a functor Ord-shaped (x ≤ y) ↦ transition map F_x → F_y. This suggests restricting prederivator-like data to posets / ordinals as a smaller test category ('maquettes'). The page is an orientation sketch at the start of the 'Champs' notes and contains no theorem.
errors: No mathematical errors can be identified; the page is schematic. The direction of the first arrow '(Ss ...) ↪ (Cat)' is ambiguous: if 'Ss Ens' means simplicial sets, the natural embedding goes the other way (nerve Cat ↪ SsEns), so the first word is probably something else (e.g. a class of small categories).

ideas.what: Encoding pasting composites of 2-cells (vertical, horizontal, interchange) by rectangular grids / products of ordinals Δ_m×Δ_n
ideas.modern_name: Joyal's Θ_2 cells [m;n_1..n_m]; grid/double-category pasting; Gray-type products of ordinals
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses globular composites and coherators, but not this grid picture as far as known

ideas.what: Cell-dimension filtration of products of ordinals: F_0=∂, F_1=Fl×∂, F_2=Fl×Fl (next page) to build a 2-categorical structure on Δ_n×Δ_n'
ideas.modern_name: cellular filtration / free 2-category on a product (Gray tensor of orientals)

ideas.what: Chain Cat ⇄ Prederivators → Ord → 'maquettes' (small test models)
ideas.modern_name: prederivators restricted to posets/ordinals; test categories

missed.claim: A program to use rectangular grids (products of ordinals) as shapes for 2-dimensional composition, linked to prederivators restricted to posets and to 'maquettes'. This anticipates Θ_2-style cell shapes and Gray-type product cells, but the page gives no developed statement.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Small historical interest: it shows Grothendieck drawing Θ_2-like cell shapes alongside prederivators. It is not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: Sketch-level pictures of standard 2-categorical pasting shapes plus a schematic chain of categories. It is mildly interesting as a precursor of Θ_2 / Gray-product combinatorics and for the term 'maquettes', but there is no new result.
